lines: Morgan Patel
+1 (555) 010-4410 | morgan.patel@example.com | example.com/code/mpatel
EDUCATION
Ridgeway University | Ph.D. candidate in Statistics | Metro City, USA | Sep 2021 - Expected May 2026
Ridgeway University | B.S. in Mathematics | Metro City, USA | Sep 2016 - May 2020
EXPERIENCE
Sunrise Bakery | Assistant Store Manager | Metro City, USA | Sep 2025 - Present
- Managed opening shifts and a team of 6 bakers and cashiers, keeping the store within its weekly labour budget.
- Ran daily stock counts and supplier orders, cutting unsold bread from 12% to 7% of production.
Northpeak Capital | Quantitative Research Intern | Metro City, USA | Jun 2025 - Aug 2025
- Improved risk-adjusted returns by 35% with a cost-aware position smoother on the desk's futures signal.
- Validated the signal on 6 years of tick data with purged walk-forward splits and an embargo period, so every backtest decision used only information available at the time.
- Wrote a feature store for 120 microstructure features with point-in-time joins, which the research team reused in two later signal projects.
- Presented the signal, its capacity estimate and failure cases to the portfolio managers, who approved a small live allocation for the next quarter.
- Selected the smoother's parameters from 400 backtested configurations and reported the best one's Sharpe as the expected live Sharpe.
- Built a short-horizon order-book imbalance signal for liquid index futures that raised the desk book's Sharpe ratio from 1.1 to 1.5 over 18 months of out-of-sample backtest after costs.
Ridgeway University | Research Assistant, Statistical Learning Lab | Metro City, USA | Jun 2020 - Aug 2021
- Cut a 2,000-run Monte Carlo study from 3 days to 5 hours by running the runs in parallel with the same random seed on every worker.
- Derived a variance bound for a sparse regression estimator; my proof tightens the previous bound by a log factor and is now Section 3 of a paper under review at JASA.
- Taught weekly recitations for 60 students in graduate probability, writing 12 problem sets and earning a 4.8/5 teaching rating.
- Released an open-source R package for high-dimensional covariance estimation with shrinkage and factor models, downloaded 3,000 times in its first year.
PROJECTS
Volatility Forecasting Study | Independent Research | Python, PyTorch | Jan 2024 - Present
- Beat a HAR-RV baseline's out-of-sample QLIKE loss by 7% on 30 equity indices with a temporal convolutional model trained on realized-volatility features.
- Tested significance with Diebold-Mariano tests across the 30 indices; after a Holm correction the forecast gain held at the 5% level on 24 of them and in both crisis periods.
- Wrote up the method, robustness checks and results as a 12-page working paper, which was presented at the department's financial econometrics seminar.
Kaggle Market Prediction Competition | Team of 3 | Python | Mar 2023 - Jun 2023
- Engineered features and trained gradient-boosting models for a market prediction competition.
- Cut validation leakage by switching to time-grouped folds, which closed a 0.02 gap between local validation and leaderboard scores.
- Added 0.4 to the Sharpe ratio of a futures book with an order-book imbalance signal, tested over 18 months out of sample.
SKILLS
Programming: Python, R, PyTorch, Kafka
Methods: time-series econometircs, high-dimensional statistics, gradient boosting

items.says: Make sure the portfolio link leads directly to a polished professional profile or code portfolio.
items.because: It should not lead to a generic landing page.

items.says: Give the link a recognizable label or domain if its destination is not obvious.
Check that linked public repositories are documented, usable, and free of proprietary material.
Verify that “Ph.D. candidate” is the institutionally correct status.
items.because: The term should be used only after formal advancement to candidacy.

items.says: Consider adding a concise research focus, dissertation area, or advisor.
items.because: It could strengthen the fit for quantitative research roles.

items.says: Use a consistent date style, preferably en dashes rather than hyphens.
items.because: An en dash is more polished.

items.says: Consider visually consolidating the repeated university name.
items.because: Both degrees are from the same university, so this could save space while preserving their distinct dates.

items.says: Put Northpeak before the bakery role and give the bakery less space.
items.because: The quant and research experience should be more prominent for quant applications.

items.says: Change “labour” to “labor.”
items.because: The résumé otherwise uses US locations and conventions.

items.says: Clarify whether staying within budget was your direct responsibility.
items.because: It could instead have been a team outcome.

items.says: Quantify the budget or how often the team met it, if possible.
items.because: The current outcome is somewhat general.

items.says: Give the measurement period for the reduction in unsold bread.
Clarify whether a process you introduced caused the reduction.
items.because: It might otherwise reflect ordinary variation.

items.says: Consider a standard waste or spoilage metric.
items.because: “Unsold bread” may not fully describe the business impact.

items.says: Check confidentiality restrictions on internal systems, performance figures, allocation decisions, and strategy details.
Name the metric meant by “risk-adjusted returns.”
items.because: The phrase is too broad without a named metric.

items.says: Give the evaluation period and sample status for the 35% result.
items.because: It is unclear whether the result was in sample, validation, or out of sample.

items.says: Clarify whether costs, turnover, and market impact were included.
Avoid implying live performance if the result came only from a backtest.
Distinguish the smoother’s result from the later signal result.
items.because: The two performance bullets may overlap.

items.says: Explain how the six years of data were divided among development, validation, and testing.
items.because: “Validated” alone may hide repeated reuse.

items.says: Check that the embargo length and purge logic matched the label horizon.
Shorten the explanatory clause if space is tight.
items.because: Quant reviewers know its purpose, while nontechnical reviewers may find it dense.

items.says: Clarify your ownership of the feature store.
items.because: It is unclear whether you designed, implemented, productionized, or maintained it.

items.says: Add scale, latency, data volume, or reliability if accurate.
Confirm that the two later projects genuinely used the feature store.
items.because: Their use is the bullet’s adoption evidence.

items.says: Clarify whether the live allocation was deployed or only approved or planned.
items.because: The internship may have ended before deployment.

items.says: Be cautious about disclosing the allocation decision.
Give this bullet lower priority if space is limited.
items.because: It is less technically valuable than the research, validation, and infrastructure bullets.

items.says: Selecting the best of 400 backtests is an overfitting and selection-bias error.
items.because: The maximum Sharpe across the configurations is optimistically biased.

items.says: Reporting the best backtested Sharpe as the expected live Sharpe is methodologically unsound.
items.because: It is not a result from data untouched by parameter selection.

items.says: Move the order-book signal result earlier within Northpeak.
items.because: It is likely the strongest Northpeak bullet.

items.says: Clarify whether the Sharpe change is incremental to an existing book or is the signal’s standalone result.
Specify whether costs include fees, spread, slippage, and market impact.
Confirm that the 18-month period was genuinely untouched out of sample.
Avoid “desk book” if testing used only a simulated portfolio.
The order-book imbalance achievement appears duplicated under the Kaggle project.
items.because: The strategy language and 18-month horizon overlap, inviting suspicion of double-counting or accidental disclosure.

items.says: Using the same random seed on every Monte Carlo worker is a critical technical problem.
items.because: Duplicate or correlated streams can reduce the effective number of simulations and invalidate uncertainty estimates.

items.says: Verify the random-number implementation and rerun the study if streams were duplicated.
items.because: The 2,000 runs must be statistically distinct for the runtime improvement to stand.

items.says: Describe reproducibility and correct parallelization rather than identical worker seeds.
Verify that the log-factor improvement is mathematically precise and supported by the paper.
Clarify your individual contribution if the paper has multiple authors.
Use the journal’s full name or abbreviation consistently.
Keep the “under review” status current and avoid implying acceptance.
Verify whether you wrote all 12 problem sets independently or contributed to them.
Give context for the 4.8/5 rating if useful and accurate.
items.because: Its response basis is not stated.

items.says: Consider giving the teaching bullet lower priority on a one-page quant résumé.
items.because: Research output may be more important.

items.says: Link the package or source repository if it is public and polished.
Specify the source and time basis of the 3,000-download count.
items.because: The count could be mistaken for cumulative downloads.

items.says: Make your personal ownership clear if others contributed.
Use “Present” only if the project is still actively developed or maintained.
items.because: Otherwise it can look indefinitely unfinished.

items.says: Link the paper and repository if they are public.
Clarify train, validation, and test separation and how model choices were made.
items.because: The test indices or periods might have influenced those choices.

items.says: Explain how the 7% improvement was summarized across indices.
items.because: It could be an average, an aggregate loss reduction, or another measure.

items.says: Confirm that the HAR-RV baseline was well tuned and used equivalent information.
State whether multiple forecast horizons are included, if applicable.
Verify that the Diebold–Mariano tests handled overlapping forecasts and serial dependence appropriately.
items.because: Those conditions affect the test assumptions and loss differentials.

items.says: Define the two crisis periods in the paper or project materials.
Clarify whether the crisis-period findings were pre-specified or exploratory.
Do not equate statistical significance with economic or practical significance.
Clarify whether you personally presented the work.
items.because: The passive construction obscures who presented it.

items.says: Describe an internal seminar accurately if it was not competitively selected.
items.because: It should not sound like an external conference acceptance.

items.says: Include the 12-page length only if it adds value.
items.because: Research quality and availability matter more than page count.

items.says: Link the paper if it is ready for review.
Name the actual competition if permitted.
items.because: The generic title makes the result difficult to verify.

items.says: Include a favorable placement, percentile, medal, or rank.
Clarify your contribution within the three-person team.
Make the features and modeling work more specific.
items.because: The bullet is too generic to distinguish your work from routine competition participation.

items.says: State the competition outcome.
Name the metric for the 0.02 gap.
items.because: Its unit is unclear.

items.says: Qualify the claim that you cut validation leakage.
items.because: A smaller local-to-leaderboard gap suggests better alignment but does not itself prove leakage was eliminated.

items.says: State whether the folds respected time order and asset or group dependencies.
The Sharpe improvement appears to duplicate the Northpeak order-book result.
items.because: The strategy type, futures context, and 18-month out-of-sample period overlap.

items.says: Explain how this result connects to the Kaggle competition.
items.because: That connection is not clear.

items.says: If the result is separate, establish distinct data, ownership, and timeframe.
items.because: Those details would distinguish it from the Northpeak work.

items.says: Check that no Northpeak intellectual property or confidential result appears in the project.
Separate programming languages from frameworks and infrastructure.
items.because: The listed items are not all the same category; PyTorch is a framework.

items.says: Remove Kafka unless you can demonstrate meaningful hands-on use.
items.because: It is not supported elsewhere on the résumé.

items.says: “Econometircs” is misspelled.
items.because: It should be “econometrics.”

items.says: Use consistent capitalization and hyphenation in the methods list.
Consider placing “gradient boosting” under a modeling-techniques category.
items.because: The skill categories should be organized consistently.

items.says: Use consistent punctuation, capitalization, and US spelling throughout.
Avoid awkward bullet breaks across lines where possible.
